variants.headline: Party leader faces a public scandal
variants.sub: The leader of {party}, {leader}, is the subject of a newly revealed scandal.
variants.body:
A scandal concerning {leader}, the leader of {party}, has come to light. The revelation makes political trust an immediate subject of public attention. An assessment of {target} must distinguish that known fact from unreported details about the conduct involved, its cause or any proceedings that might follow.

A leader, a scandal, and a story everyone can be tempted to improve in the telling. Resist the temptation. The revelation is news enough. Readers deserve a sharp question about trust, not a collection of invented details dressed up as the delicious part of the story.

In our judgment, {target} does not deserve confidence in this matter. Political trust requires a demanding standard, and the scandal is an appropriate occasion for a distinctly critical assessment. Readers deserve a clear story and a straight answer about responsibility.
